dedupe_keys.name: explainable machine learning and spatial clustering for road network condition analysis a case study of ecuador s state highways using open government data

description: Luis Leonardo Zambrano-Salazar publishes Python analysis code for Ecuador’s state highway condition. Zenodo lists source, requirements and a public README under MIT at no cost. The workflow reads MTOP road geometry and condition records plus national traffic counts, calculates global and local spatial clustering, fits a Random Forest with SHAP explanations and exports a labelled GeoJSON for QGIS. It can test how traffic and spatial conditions relate to poor road segments when planning maintenance scenarios. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. A limitation is that the government input datasets are not redistributed; users must obtain current exports and match the documented filenames and road codes. Statistical association is not proof of deterioration cause, and source vintages can change. The script was not downloaded or run, and neither model fit nor mapped clusters were reproduced.
